submission.causalMechanism: HostAssigned driver's run_turn constructs the persisted conclusion dict with a hard-coded empty unresolved_unknowns list (host_assigned.py:688) and the system prompt instructs the model to emit empty unresolved_unknowns (line 369), so any Harness-side unresolved uncertainty is discarded at the Security-owned completion-record layer rather than preserved.
submission.hypothesis: In host_assigned.py at line 685-689, when the Host records a candidate_completed run, it unconditionally hard-codes `"unresolved_unknowns": []` into the conclusion dictionary that is persisted via lifecycle.record_run. This discards any unresolved uncertainty that the Harness may have surfaced in its conclusion trace, because the recorded conclusion is constructed from only `evidence.rationale` (summary) and a literal empty list, rather than forwarding the actual unresolved_unknowns from the Harness conclusion. The system prompt (lines 367-370) additionally instructs the model to force unresolved_unknowns to an empty array, so any genuine unresolved uncertainty is flattened into caveats in the summary text. The narrow Security-owned representation path that loses the uncertainty is the conclusion recording step at host_assigned.py:685-690 where the `conclusion` dict with `"unresolved_unknowns": []` is built and handed to lifecycle.record_run for Host-assigned completion, separate from Harness core semantics.
submission.nextFalsifier: Check whether the Harness conclusion object (result.conclusion) actually carries an unresolved_unknowns field, and verify that lifecycle.record_run or HarnessHost is the Security-owned layer where the empty list is injected; also inspect agent_stack.py AgentTurnEvidence to see whether the field is even represented in the evidence model.
